subject: environmental-science
title: Demographic Transition Stages
welcome_lead: From high-stationary to low-stationary — five stages of population change.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on the demographic transition model.
final_note: Demography is destiny — and education is the most powerful population policy.

concepts.def: High birth and death rates; stable, low population (pre-industrial).
Death rate falls (sanitation, medicine); rapid population growth.
Birth rate falls (education, urbanisation); slowing growth.
Low birth and death rates; population stabilises.
Birth rate below death rate; population decline (e.g., Japan, Italy).
Average children per woman; replacement level ~2.1.

walkthroughs.body_html: The DTM tracks crude birth/death rates over time. Most LICs sit in stages 2–3; HICs in stage 4 or 5.
Falling child mortality, female literacy, urbanisation and access to contraception drive birth-rate decline.
Sub-replacement TFR raises dependency ratios and labour-market strain. Pro-natal policies have limited success.
